risks: Root integration can change inspected shared files after hashing; report is generation-bound, not a completion or immutable committed-baseline receipt.

Frozen Groma source citations provide hashes but not independently inspected parser/scanner bytes. Inventing nested wire keys or ownership rules would be incompatible with the required experimental OKF contract.

Generic registry readiness can conflate importer compatibility with optional scanner availability; treating both as one ready flag would wrongly block read-only import or falsely promise scanner coverage.
Pure RepositoryScope/binding checks do not authenticate a current actor; import must consume CI-002 host authority, not trust renderer-supplied workspace/root.
C4 records cannot safely be squeezed into current CodeSymbol/CodeEdge enums; source provenance projection alone does not preserve C4 lifecycle/ownership/trust semantics.
Ancestor/container/component ownership interpretation and canonical duplicate claims require actual frozen reconciliation rules; last-writer conflict resolution loses user-visible errors.

CI-008 explicitly depends on CI-005 but owns artifacts/freshness needed for integrated publication. Adding it as an upstream DAG edge creates a cycle; lead must agree the handoff before implementation and retain downstream integration gates.

No durable architecture store or existing live C4 surface was proven by this inspection. A pure importer and passing unit tests alone cannot satisfy published persistence, stale-state and conflict-surfacing claims.
Implicit groma init/scan/watch/export or dependency repair can mutate OKF/user instructions; unsupported runtime must remain an explicit outcome, not an automatic install or simulated adapter.

Raw scanner calls are ephemeral and must not be silently promoted into persistent full-call-graph or deterministic-supported evidence. Dirty source bytes must not receive exact parent-commit citations.

Actual scanner/runtime/license readiness, EG-IDENTITY, repository/egress policy and native tool transport receipts remain unverified; provider inventory, historical installation and worker final text cannot replace them.
